e00.title: The Lost Garden
e00.subtitle: A road closed, and a first promise
story: God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, and breathed the breath of life into the nostrils of a man shaped from the dust. The man opened his eyes. Soon Eve stood beside him, and the two of them walked through a garden heavy with fruit, lovely to look at and good to eat. But of one tree standing in the middle of the garden, God said this. The fruit of the tree that gives knowledge of good and evil, that alone you must not eat. On the day you eat it, you will surely die.

Then the serpent came close to Eve and whispered. Did God really say you may not eat from any tree in the garden? Eve answered that only the tree in the middle was forbidden. Then the serpent said, you will not die. Eat it, and your eyes will be opened, and you will know good and evil, like God. Eve looked up at the tree. It was beautiful, and it seemed it could make her wise. She picked the fruit and ate, and she handed some to Adam, who was beside her. Then the eyes of both were opened, and they knew that they were naked. When they heard the footsteps of God in the evening breeze, they hid among the trees.

Adam, where are you? Trembling with fear, the two came out, and each laid the blame on the other, and on the serpent. That day sin came in between people and God, and death followed close behind. God declared to the serpent, the woman's offspring will crush your head. Then he made garments of skin and clothed them, and sent them out of the garden. East of the garden, cherubim and a flaming sword that turned every way guarded the road to the tree of life. The story of opening that closed road again now begins with a girl in Nazareth.

words.text: You may eat freely from any tree in the garden. But do not eat from the tree that gives knowledge of good and evil, for on the day you eat from it you will certainly die.
Where are you?
I will set hostility between you and the woman, between your offspring and hers. Her offspring will crush your head, and you will bite his heel.

e00.note: Genesis 3:15 has long been called the “first gospel”. The New Testament finds in Jesus Christ the answer to who the woman’s offspring is that crushes the serpent’s head. Paul called him “the last Adam”.
e00.reflect: After they sinned, Adam and Eve hid among the trees, and God called out, “Where are you?” When I have done wrong, am I the one who hides from him, or the one who answers his call?
e00.credit: Giovanni di Paolo, The Creation of the World and the Expulsion from Paradise, 1445 (detail) · The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Public domain

e01.title: The Annunciation
e01.subtitle: A story that began with a girl's yes
story: Nazareth, a small village leaning against the hills of Galilee. In this town, never once named anywhere in the Old Testament, lived a girl named Mary, promised in marriage to Joseph of the house of David. On a day like any other, a dazzling light stood before her. It was the angel Gabriel, sent from God.

Rejoice, you who are so richly favored. The Lord is with you. Mary was startled and shrank back. Do not be afraid, Mary. You will bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus. He will sit on the throne of David and reign forever, and his kingdom will have no end. Nothing is impossible for God. After a long silence, Mary bowed her head. I am the Lord's servant. Let it happen to me just as you have said.

When Joseph learned that Mary, his betrothed, was with child, he was a righteous man and did not want to shame her, so he resolved to end the engagement quietly. That night, as he slept with the thought on his mind, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream. Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife. The child in her was conceived by the Holy Spirit. Joseph woke and took Mary as his wife, just as the angel had told him. While the world knew nothing of it, heaven was beginning its greatest story in the lowest of places.

words.text: Do not be afraid, Mary. God has shown you his favor. Nothing is impossible for God.
I am the Lord's servant. Let it happen to me just as you have said.
Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife. Name the son Jesus, for he will rescue his people from their sins.

e01.note: Nazareth is thought to have been a small farming village of only a few hundred people. It was so obscure that in John's Gospel Nathanael asks, 'Can anything good come out of Nazareth?'
e01.reflect: Without understanding it all, Mary answered, “May it happen to me as you have said.” Faced with a will of God that differs from my plans, what answer am I giving?

quiz.q: What name did the angel give Mary for her child?
quiz.explain: 'Jesus' means 'the Lord saves' (Lk 1:31; Mt 1:21). 'Immanuel' is a title from the prophecy of Isaiah that Matthew quotes.

e01.credit: James Tissot, The Annunciation, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e02.title: Night in Bethlehem
e02.subtitle: A night with no room, a song over the fields
story: A single line from the emperor set a whole empire on the road. To be registered, everyone had to go to the town of their ancestors. Joseph left Nazareth with Mary, whose time to give birth was near. Over hills and through valleys they finally reached Bethlehem, and it was already crowded with people.

At every door they knocked on, the answer was the same. No room. In the end, the place where they lay down was where the animals were kept. That night Mary gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped the baby snugly in cloth and laid him in a feeding trough. In the cold air, a small breath rose white.

At the same hour, out in the fields beyond the town, shepherds were keeping watch over their flocks through the night. Suddenly the sky grew bright as noon. As they fell to the ground in fear, an angel spoke to them. Today in the town of David a Savior has been born for you. Then a great heavenly army appeared and sang. Glory to God in the highest, and on earth, peace. The shepherds ran through the dark and found the baby lying in the manger. As they told what they had heard, Mary said nothing, and kept all these things in her heart.

words.text: Do not be afraid. I bring you good news that will be great joy for all the people. Today in the town of David your Savior is born, Christ the Lord.
Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace to the people in whom he delights.
Come, let us go to Bethlehem and see with our own eyes this thing the Lord has made known to us.

e02.note: The Greek word 'kataluma', usually rendered 'inn', can also mean the guest room of a family home. So some interpret Jesus as being born on the lower floor of a house where livestock were kept, or in a cave.
e02.reflect: On the first night the Savior came, the news went first to shepherds in the fields, and they hurried off to find the baby. When was the last time I hurried to meet that child?

quiz.q: What sign did the angel give the shepherds?
options: A star resting over a house
A prince born in a palace
A baby wrapped in cloth, lying in a manger
A lamb offered at the Temple
quiz.explain: The angel said the sign would be 'a baby wrapped in cloth and lying in a manger' (Lk 2:12). The star belongs to Matthew's account of the Magi.

e02.credit: James Tissot, The Adoration of the Shepherds, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e03.title: Simeon and Anna in the Temple
e03.subtitle: A light in the eyes of two who waited a lifetime
story: On the eighth day after his birth, the baby was circumcised and given the name Jesus, the very name the angel had spoken. When the days of purification were complete, Joseph and Mary carried the baby up to the temple in Jerusalem, to offer what the law required, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.

Just then, led by the Spirit, an old man came into the temple courts. It was Simeon, a righteous and devout man. He had lived holding on to a promise, that he would not die before he had seen the Lord's Christ. Simeon took the baby into his arms and praised God. Lord, now you let your servant go in peace. My eyes have seen your salvation. Then he looked at Mary and said, a sword will pierce your own heart too.

An aged widow named Anna came up to them as well. She was a prophet, the daughter of Phanuel of the tribe of Asher, eighty-four years old. She never left the temple, and spent her years fasting and praying night and day. When she saw the child, her face lit up. She gave thanks to God and told about this child to everyone who was waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.

words.text: Lord, now let your servant go in peace, as you promised. My eyes have seen your salvation.
This child will cause many to fall and many to rise. And your own heart will ache as if pierced by a sword.

e03.note: Leviticus 12 allows a family of limited means to offer two birds instead of a lamb. That Joseph and Mary offered birds shows that this was a poor family.
e03.reflect: After a lifetime of waiting, Simeon and Anna recognized the baby Jesus. When I have waited long and still see no answer, what keeps me in the place of prayer?

quiz.q: From which tribe was the prophet Anna, who met the infant Jesus in the Temple?
quiz.explain: Anna was the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher (Lk 2:36).

e03.credit: James Tissot, The Aged Simeon, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e04.title: The Magi Follow the Star
e04.subtitle: Men from the far east who read the stars
story: In the days when Herod was king, travelers who had come a long way appeared in the streets of Jerusalem. They were wise men from the east. Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star in the east and have come to worship him. When word of this reached the palace, King Herod was deeply troubled, and all Jerusalem was stirred along with him.

Herod called together all the chief priests and teachers of the law. Where is the Christ to be born? They answered. In Bethlehem of Judea. That is what the prophet wrote. The king secretly called the wise men aside and questioned them closely about when the star had appeared. Then he sent them to Bethlehem and said, go and search carefully for the child. When you find him, let me know, so that I too may go and worship him.

As the wise men set out, the star they had seen in the east went ahead of them again, until it came to rest over the place where the child was. The wise men were overjoyed. Entering the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother, and they bowed down and worshiped him. They opened their treasure chests and offered gold, frankincense, and myrrh. Then, warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, they returned to their own country by another road.

words.text: Where is the one born king of the Jews? We saw his star rising and have come to worship him.

words.who: The chief priests and teachers of the Law
words.text: Bethlehem in the land of Judah, you are by no means a small town. From you will come a leader who will shepherd my people Israel.
Go and search carefully for the child, and when you find him, report to me, so that I may go and worship him too.

e04.note: The 'magoi' were likely a class of scholars who studied the stars in Persia or Babylonia. Scripture does not say how many there were; the tradition of three comes from the three gifts.
e04.reflect: At the end of a long road, the Magi bowed before the child and offered their most precious gifts. What would I gladly offer Jesus today?

quiz.q: Which of these was NOT a gift the Magi gave the child Jesus?
quiz.explain: The Magi offered gold, frankincense, and myrrh (Mt 2:11). The thirty pieces of silver were the money Judas later received.

e04.credit: James Tissot, The Magi Journeying, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e05.title: Flight into Egypt
e05.subtitle: Escape by night, and weeping in Ramah
story: After the wise men had gone, an angel of the Lord appeared again to Joseph in a dream. Get up, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt. Herod is searching for the child to destroy him. Stay there until I tell you. Joseph got up at once. That very night he took the child and Mary and set off into the darkness.

The family went south, down the dry road into Egypt. In that strange land far from home, they stayed until Herod died, until the word came to leave again. On this flight, Matthew recalls one old line from the prophet Hosea. Out of Egypt I called my son.

Meanwhile Herod, realizing that the wise men had outwitted him, flew into a rage. He reckoned from the time he had learned from the wise men, and sent his men. In Bethlehem and all the country around it, every boy two years old and under was killed. Throughout the town, the wailing of mothers broke out. A voice is heard in Ramah. Rachel weeping for her children. She refuses to be comforted, because they are no more.

words.text: Get up, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, for Herod is searching for the child to destroy him.
A voice is heard in Ramah, weeping and bitter mourning. Rachel weeps for her children and will not be comforted, because they are no more.

e05.note: Alexandria in Egypt had a large Jewish community at the time, making it a natural refuge. Bethlehem was a small town, so the children killed probably numbered a few dozen or fewer.
e05.reflect: Joseph got up that very night and set out. He had not been told everything, yet he trusted the word. Is there some obedience I know I owe but keep putting off these days?

quiz.q: Herod ordered the killing of boys in Bethlehem under what age?
quiz.explain: Based on the time he had learned from the Magi, Herod killed all the boys two years old and under (Mt 2:16).

e05.credit: James Tissot, The Flight into Egypt, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e06.title: Return to Nazareth
e06.subtitle: A child growing up in an unknown village
story: Herod was dead. In Egypt, an angel of the Lord appeared once more to Joseph in a dream. Get up, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel. Those who sought the child's life are dead. Joseph got up, took the child and Mary, and set out again on the long road.

But on the way, news reached him. Archelaus, Herod's son, was ruling Judea in his father's place. Joseph was afraid to go there. Warned again in a dream, he turned north to Galilee and settled in a small town called Nazareth. So the words of the prophets came true, that he would be called a Nazarene.

In the little village on the hill, the child grew. Day by day he grew taller and stronger. He was filled with wisdom, and the grace of God rested on him. Luke tells of those long years in only a few words. The sun rose and set and rose again, and quiet years went by, far from the eyes of the world.

words.text: Get up, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel. Those who wanted the child dead are gone.
The child grew and became strong, full of wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.

e06.note: Herod the Great is thought to have died around 4 BC, after which Archelaus ruled Judea and Herod Antipas ruled Galilee. Archelaus ruled so harshly that Rome removed him in AD 6.
e06.reflect: The Son of God grew up quietly for many years in an ordinary home in Nazareth. Can I believe that my own unnoticed days are also a time of growing before God?

quiz.q: Joseph was afraid to go to Judea because of who was ruling there?
quiz.explain: Joseph was afraid when he heard that Archelaus, Herod's son, was ruling Judea in his father's place (Mt 2:22).

e06.credit: James Tissot, The Return from Egypt, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e07.title: Twelve, in His Father's House
e07.subtitle: The boy found after three days, in his Father's house
story: Every year when Passover came, Joseph and Mary went up to Jerusalem. The year Jesus turned twelve, they went on the pilgrimage as was the custom. When the feast was over, people turned for home. Thinking the boy was somewhere among their company, his parents walked a full day's journey. All the while, the boy Jesus had stayed behind in Jerusalem.

But however hard they searched among their relatives and friends, the boy was nowhere to be found. Frantic, his parents went back to Jerusalem, and after three days they found their son in the temple. He was sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions. Everyone who heard him was amazed at his understanding and his answers.

His mother came to him and said, child, why have you done this to us? Your father and I have been searching for you in such distress. Jesus answered. Why were you looking for me? Didn't you know I had to be in my Father's house? His parents did not understand what he meant. He went down with them to Nazareth and lived in obedience to them. Mary treasured all these things in her heart. And Jesus grew in wisdom and in stature, and in favor with God and with people.

words.text: Why were you looking for me? Didn't you know I had to be in my Father's house?
Child, why have you done this to us? Your father and I have been searching for you in such distress.

e07.note: Galileans made the pilgrimage in large village caravans, so a child's absence could go unnoticed for a day. Nazareth to Jerusalem was a walk of three or four days.
e07.reflect: At twelve, Jesus said, “Didn't you know I had to be in my Father's house?” For me, is my Father's side a place I must be, or somewhere I drop by now and then?

quiz.q: After how many days did Joseph and Mary find Jesus in the Temple?
quiz.explain: After three days his parents found Jesus in the Temple, sitting among the teachers (Lk 2:46).

e07.credit: James Tissot, Jesus Found in the Temple, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e08.title: Baptism in the Jordan
e08.subtitle: Heaven opened above the river
story: The banks of the Jordan were crowded with people who had come for the baptism of repentance. Into that crowd walked a man from Nazareth in Galilee. It was Jesus, about thirty years old. As he came near, John the Baptist tried hard to stop him. I need to be baptized by you, and yet you come to me?

Jesus answered. Let it be so for now. It is right for us to fulfill all righteousness this way. At that, John stopped resisting. The water of the Jordan covered his body and streamed away. As Jesus came up out of the water and was praying, the heavens opened.

The Spirit of God came down like a dove and rested on him. In that moment, when even the sound of the river seemed to fade, a voice rang out from heaven. You are my beloved Son. In you I take delight. The carpenter of Nazareth, who had lived so quietly, was now stepping out before the world.

words.text: Let it be this way for now. It is right for us to do this and so fulfill all that God's righteousness requires.
You are my Son, whom I love. In you I take great delight.

e08.note: John's Gospel calls the place where John was baptizing 'Bethany beyond the Jordan'. It is thought to be Al-Maghtas, on the Jordan east of Jericho. Luke gives Jesus' age at this time as about thirty.
e08.reflect: Before Jesus had done anything at all, heaven said, “You are my beloved Son.” Can I believe in that love even on days when I have accomplished nothing?

quiz.q: When Jesus was baptized, the Spirit came down like what?
quiz.explain: The Spirit of God descended like a dove and rested on him (Mt 3:16; Mk 1:10; Lk 3:22).

e08.credit: James Tissot, The Baptism of Jesus, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e09.title: Forty Days in the Wilderness
e09.subtitle: Three temptations overcome in a starving body
story: Before the water of his baptism had even dried, the Spirit led Jesus out into the wilderness. It was a land of nothing but rock and sand, where the sun baked the stones by day. Wild animals came and went around him. For forty days and forty nights he ate nothing. When his body was sinking with hunger, the tempter came.

If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread. The devil took him to the holy city and set him on the highest point of the temple. Throw yourself down. Isn't it written that angels will lift you up in their hands? Then he took him to a very high mountain and spread out before him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory. Bow down and worship me, and I will give you all of this.

Each time, Jesus answered with the words of scripture. A person does not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God. Do not put the Lord your God to the test. Away with you, Satan. Worship the Lord your God and serve him only. When the devil left him, angels came and took care of him. Luke adds that the devil withdrew for a while, waiting for another chance.

words.text: It is written: people do not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.
Away with you, Satan! It is written: worship the Lord your God, and serve him alone.
It is also written: do not put the Lord your God to the test.

e09.note: The Judean wilderness is a dry stretch of limestone hills running from east of Jerusalem down to the Dead Sea. Matthew and Luke give the second and third temptations in a different order.
e09.reflect: Each time he was tested in the wilderness, Jesus answered with Scripture: “It is written.” In a shaky moment, what is the first thing that comes out of my mouth?

quiz.q: In the first temptation, what did the devil tell Jesus to turn the stones into?
quiz.explain: The devil said that if he were the Son of God, he should command the stones to become bread (Mt 4:3; Lk 4:3).

e09.credit: James Tissot, Jesus Tempted in the Wilderness, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e10.title: Come and See: The First Disciples
e10.subtitle: An invitation at four in the afternoon
story: Bethany beyond the Jordan. John, who only the day before had cried out that Jesus was the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world, was standing with two of his disciples when Jesus passed by, and he pointed to him. Look, the Lamb of God. Hearing this, the two disciples quietly followed him. Jesus turned and asked them, what are you looking for?

Rabbi, where are you staying? He answered. Come and see. The two went with him and saw where he was staying. It was about four in the afternoon. Andrew, one of the two who spent that day with him, went straight to find his brother Simon. We have found the Messiah. Jesus looked at Simon and said, you are Simon, son of John. From now on I will call you Cephas.

The next day, as he was about to leave for Galilee, Jesus found Philip of Bethsaida and called him. Follow me. Philip went to find Nathanael and told him the news. We have found the one Moses and the prophets wrote about, Jesus of Nazareth. Nathanael asked back, can anything good come out of Nazareth? He was unimpressed, but when Jesus said he had seen him under the fig tree, he gave way completely and confessed. Rabbi, you are the Son of God.

words.text: What are you looking for? Come and see.
You are Simon, son of John. From now on you will be called Cephas.
Before Philip called you, while you were under the fig tree, I saw you.
Teacher, you are the Son of God. You are the King of Israel!
Look! Here is God’s Lamb, who carries away the sin of the world.

e10.note: 'The tenth hour' counts from sunrise in the Jewish way, so it means about four in the afternoon. 'Cephas' is Aramaic for rock; in Greek it is 'Peter'.
e10.reflect: After meeting Jesus, Andrew first went to find his brother Simon and told him, “We have found the Messiah.” Who is the person I want to say “Come and see” to?

quiz.q: What new name did Jesus give Simon, Andrew's brother?
quiz.explain: Jesus told Simon he would be called 'Cephas', which is translated 'Peter' (Jn 1:42).

e10.credit: James Tissot, The Calling of Saint John and Saint Andrew, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e11.title: The Wedding at Cana
e11.subtitle: The first sign, water turned to wine
story: There was a wedding feast at Cana in Galilee. The mother of Jesus was there, and Jesus and his disciples had been invited too. The house was crowded with people who had come to celebrate. Just as the laughter and songs were at their height, the servants' faces went stiff. The wine had run out.

His mother came to Jesus and said quietly, they have no more wine. Jesus answered. Mother, what does that have to do with me? My hour has not yet come. Even so, his mother told the servants, do whatever he tells you. Six large stone jars stood there, the kind used for Jewish purification rites.

Jesus said to the servants, fill the jars with water. The servants filled every jar to the brim. Now draw some out and take it to the master of the feast. He tasted the water that had become wine, not knowing where it had come from, and called the bridegroom. Everyone serves the good wine first, but you have saved the good wine until now. This was the first sign Jesus did. His glory was revealed, and his disciples believed in him.

words.text: Fill the jars with water. Now draw some out and take it to the master of the feast.
Mother, what does that have to do with me? My hour has not yet come.
Whatever he tells you, do it.

e11.note: Wedding feasts then could last up to a week, and running out of wine was a great shame for the family. Each jar is thought to have held two or three metretes, roughly 80 to 120 liters.
e11.reflect: Without knowing why, the servants did as Jesus said and filled the jars to the brim with water. Could I obey like that, filling the jars?

quiz.q: How many stone jars stood at the wedding feast in Cana?
quiz.explain: There were six stone jars used for purification rites (Jn 2:6).

e11.credit: James Tissot, The Marriage at Cana, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e12.title: Overturning the Temple Tables
e12.subtitle: His Father's house turned into a market
story: As Passover drew near, Jesus went up to Jerusalem. When he entered the temple courts, merchants selling cattle, sheep, and doves stood in rows. Money changers sat at their tables exchanging coins. The bellowing of animals and the clink of money filled the place meant for prayer.

Jesus made a whip out of cords. He drove all the sheep and cattle out of the temple, scattered the money changers' coins, and overturned their tables. To those selling doves he said, get these out of here. Do not turn my Father's house into a marketplace. Watching him, his disciples remembered a line from the Psalms. Zeal for your house will consume me.

The Jewish leaders crowded around and challenged him. What sign will you show us for doing this? Jesus answered. Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up again. They shot back. It took forty-six years to build this temple, and you will raise it in three days? But the temple he spoke of was his own body. Only after he had risen from the dead did his disciples remember these words and believe.

words.text: Get these out of here. Stop turning my Father's house into a place of trade.
Tear down this temple, and in three days I will raise it up again.
This Temple took forty-six years to build, and you will raise it in three days?

e12.note: Herod began rebuilding the Temple around 20 BC. The money changers exchanged coins from many lands into Tyrian shekels for paying the Temple tax. John places this event early in Jesus' ministry.
e12.reflect: Jesus cleansed the temple, saying, “Stop turning my Father's house into a marketplace.” Is there some calculation mixed into the heart with which I come to God?

quiz.q: How many years did the Jewish leaders say it had taken to build the Temple?
quiz.explain: They said, 'This Temple has been under construction for forty-six years' (Jn 2:20).

e12.credit: James Tissot, The Merchants Chased from the Temple, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e13.title: Nicodemus Comes by Night
e13.subtitle: The secret of the wind, heard in the dark
story: Only when the night was deep did a man come quietly to see Jesus. It was Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a leader of the Jews. Seated across from him where a single lamp flickered, he spoke carefully. Teacher, we know you are a teacher who has come from God. No one could do the signs you do unless God were with him.

Jesus answered. Truly I tell you, unless a person is born anew, he cannot see the kingdom of God. Nicodemus did not understand. How can someone be born when he is old? Jesus said again. Unless a person is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. The wind blows wherever it pleases. You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.

The words went on deep into the night. Just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up. God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him will not perish but have eternal life. The light has come into the world, but people loved darkness rather than light. Those words lingered long in the stillness of the night.

words.text: I tell you the truth: unless someone is born anew from above, they cannot see the kingdom of God.
God loved the world so much that he gave his only Son, so that all who believe in him will not perish but have eternal life.
The wind blows where it wills. You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with all who are born of the Spirit.

e13.note: The Greek word 'anothen', rendered 'anew', means both 'again' and 'from above'. Nicodemus appears again later at Jesus' burial, bringing myrrh and aloes.
e13.reflect: Nicodemus came to Jesus at night, away from people's eyes, and heard that he must be born again. Do I stop at knowing about Jesus, or am I truly living as someone born anew?

quiz.q: When Jesus said the Son of Man must be lifted up, he compared it to what Moses lifted up in the wilderness. What was it?
quiz.explain: He said that just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up (Jn 3:14; Num 21:9).

e13.credit: James Tissot, Interview between Jesus and Nicodemus, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e14.title: The Well at Sychar
e14.subtitle: Noon at the well, two thirsty people
story: On the way from Judea to Galilee, Jesus passed through Samaria and came to a town called Sychar. It was near the land Jacob had long ago given to his son Joseph, where Jacob's well was. Tired from the long road, he simply sat down by the well. It was around noon, with the sun hanging overhead. His disciples had gone into the town to buy food.

Then a Samaritan woman came to draw water. Jesus said, give me a drink. Startled, the woman asked back, you are a Jew, and I am a Samaritan woman. How can you ask me for a drink? Jesus answered. Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again, but whoever drinks the water I give will never thirst again. The conversation turned to her five husbands, and then to the question of where one ought to worship.

The woman said, when the Messiah, the one called Christ, comes, he will explain everything to us. Jesus said, I am he, the one speaking to you. The woman left her water jar behind and ran into the town. There is a man who told me everything I ever did. The Samaritans came out in crowds and begged him to stay, and he stayed there two days. The people confessed. This man truly is the Savior of the world.

words.text: Whoever drinks this water will thirst again. Whoever drinks the water I give will never thirst; it becomes in them a spring welling up to eternal life.
God is spirit, so those who worship him must worship in spirit and in truth.
My food is to do the will of the one who sent me and to carry his work through to the end.
Come and see! There is a man who told me everything I ever did. Could this be the Christ?

e14.note: Samaritans worshiped on Mount Gerizim rather than in Jerusalem, and there was deep hostility between them and the Jews. Jacob's well, which still survives near modern Nablus, is said to be about 40 meters deep.
e14.reflect: At the well, Jesus told the woman he would give her water that would leave her never thirsty again. These days, where am I taking the thirst that nothing seems to fill?

quiz.q: At the Samaritans' request, how long did Jesus stay in Sychar?
quiz.explain: When the Samaritans asked him to stay, Jesus remained there two days (Jn 4:40).

e14.credit: James Tissot, The Woman of Samaria at the Well, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e15.title: Life from Afar
e15.subtitle: A father who turned back trusting a single word
story: After two days in Samaria, Jesus set out again for Galilee. Though he himself had said that a prophet is not honored in his own country, the people of Galilee welcomed him, for they had seen everything he had done at the festival in Jerusalem. He came again to Cana, where the water had become wine.

Hearing the news, a royal official came hurrying up from Capernaum, out of breath. At home his son lay dying of a fever. He came down and begged Jesus to heal his son, and Jesus said, unless you people see signs and wonders, you will not believe. The official pleaded again. Lord, come down before my child dies. Jesus said to him, go. Your son will live.

The man believed the word and set off. On his way down, his servants came running from the house to meet him. The boy is alive. He asked, when did he begin to get better? The servants answered. Yesterday, at the seventh hour, the fever left him. It was the very hour Jesus had said, your son will live. He and his whole household believed.

words.text: Go. Your son will live.
Unless you see signs and wonders, you will never believe.
Lord, please come down before my child dies.

e15.note: Cana to Capernaum is about 25 kilometers, a road that descends to the shore of the Sea of Galilee, below sea level. The seventh hour is about one in the afternoon, and John calls this the second sign Jesus performed in Galilee.
e15.reflect: The royal official held on to a single sentence, “Your son will live,” and turned for home. Is there a road for me right now that I must walk holding only his word, before I see anything?

quiz.q: According to the servants, when did the official's son's fever break?
quiz.explain: The servants said, 'The fever left him yesterday at the seventh hour', the very hour when Jesus had said, 'Your son will live' (Jn 4:52–53).

e15.credit: James Tissot, The Healing of the Officer's Son, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e16.title: Rejected in Nazareth
e16.subtitle: Those closest to him were the first to turn away
story: On the Sabbath, Jesus came back to Nazareth, the town where he had grown up, and went into the synagogue as he always did. When he stood up to read, the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. He unrolled it and found a certain passage. The Spirit of the Lord is upon me. He has sent me to bring good news to the poor and to proclaim freedom to the captives.

He rolled up the scroll, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down, and every eye in the synagogue was fixed on him. Then he began to speak. Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing. The people marveled at the gracious words coming from his mouth, and yet they murmured. Isn't this Joseph's son?

Jesus said, no prophet is welcome in his hometown. Elijah was sent to none of the many widows in Israel, but to a widow in Zarephath in the land of Sidon, and in the time of Elisha, only Naaman the Syrian was made clean. The synagogue boiled with rage. They drove him out of the town and dragged him to the edge of the cliff on which the town was built, meaning to throw him down. But he passed right through the middle of them and went on his way.

words.text: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me. He has sent me to bring good news to the poor, release to captives, and sight to the blind.
This scripture you have just heard with your own ears is fulfilled here today.
I tell you the truth: no prophet is welcomed in his own hometown.

e16.note: Synagogue worship included readings from the Law and then the Prophets, and it was customary to sit down to teach after reading. That is why every eye was on Jesus when he returned the scroll and sat down.
e16.reflect: The people of his hometown said, “Isn't this Joseph's son?” and would not accept Jesus. Are there words of his I let slip by because they have grown too familiar?

quiz.q: Which prophet's scroll was Jesus handed to read in the synagogue at Nazareth?
quiz.explain: Luke records that the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to Jesus (Lk 4:17). The passage he read was the opening of Isaiah 61.

e16.credit: James Tissot, Jesus Unrolls the Book in the Synagogue, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e17.title: Fishers of People
e17.subtitle: A single word dropped over empty nets
story: On the shore of the lake of Gennesaret, two empty boats were pulled up at the water's edge. The fishermen, who had caught nothing all night, had stepped out and were washing their nets. As the crowd pressed in to hear the word, Jesus got into Simon's boat. He asked him to push out a little from the shore, then sat in the boat and taught the people on the beach.

When he had finished teaching, Jesus said to Simon, put out into the deep water and let down your nets for a catch. Simon answered. Master, we worked hard all night and caught nothing. But because you say so, I will let down the nets. As the nets sank into the water, fish swarmed in until the nets were close to tearing. They waved to their partners in the other boat, and both boats were filled until they began to sink.

Simon Peter fell down at the knees of Jesus. Lord, go away from me. I am a sinful man. Jesus said, do not be afraid. From now on you will be catching people. Simon and Andrew, and James and John the sons of Zebedee, brought their boats to shore, left everything behind, and followed him.

words.text: Come, follow me. I will make you into people who fish for others.
Row out into the deep water, and let down your nets for a catch.
Do not be afraid. From now on you will be bringing in people.
Lord, go away from me. I am a sinful man.

e17.note: In 1986 a fishing boat about eight meters long was found in the mud on the shore of the Sea of Galilee. Dated to around the time of Jesus, it gives a sense of the size of the boats fishermen used then.
e17.reflect: After a fruitless night, Simon said, “Because you say so, I will let down the nets,” and went back out on the water. Is there something my experience says won't work, but I should try because he said so?

quiz.q: Who was the father of James and John, who were called while mending nets in their boat?
quiz.explain: James and John left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men and followed Jesus (Mk 1:19–20).

e17.credit: James Tissot, The Miraculous Draught of Fishes, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e18.title: A Long Day in Capernaum
e18.subtitle: From synagogue to doorstep, and prayer before dawn
story: On the Sabbath, the voice of Jesus rang through the synagogue in Capernaum. The people were amazed at his teaching, because unlike the teachers of the law, he went straight to the heart, like one with authority. Just then a man possessed by an unclean spirit cried out. Jesus of Nazareth, have you come to destroy us? I know who you are. You are the Holy One of God.

Jesus rebuked him. Be silent, and come out of him. The unclean spirit shook the man violently, gave a loud cry, and left him. Leaving the synagogue, they went straight to the house of Simon and Andrew. Simon's mother-in-law was lying sick with a fever. Jesus went to her, took her by the hand and lifted her up, and the fever left her, and at once she got up and served them.

When the sun went down and the Sabbath was over, the whole town came crowding to the door, bringing the sick and those possessed by demons. Jesus laid his hands on each one and healed them. The next day, while it was still dark, he went out alone to a deserted place and prayed. Simon and his companions came after him and said, everyone is looking for you. Jesus answered. Let us go on to the other villages. I must proclaim the message there too.

words.text: Let us go on to the nearby towns. I must bring the message there too. This is what I came out to do.
Be silent, and come out of him.
Everyone is looking for you.

e18.note: The white limestone synagogue standing in Capernaum today was built in the fourth or fifth century. The black basalt foundation beneath it is thought to be the remains of the synagogue of Jesus' day.
e18.reflect: The morning after crowds had pressed in all day, Jesus went off alone before dawn to pray. In my busy day, where is the time I spend alone with God?

quiz.q: In the house they visited after leaving the synagogue, who was healed of a fever?
quiz.explain: Jesus took Simon's mother-in-law by the hand and raised her up, the fever left her, and she got up and served them (Mk 1:30–31; Lk 4:38–39).

e18.credit: James Tissot, The Healing of Peter's Mother-in-law, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e19.title: The Day the Roof Opened
e19.subtitle: The faith of friends opened the roof
story: As word spread that Jesus had come back to Capernaum, the house filled with people in no time. There was no room left, not even outside the door. Pharisees and teachers of the law who had come from the villages of Galilee and Judea, and from Jerusalem, were sitting there too. Jesus was speaking the word to them.

Just then four men came carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. Blocked by the crowd, they could not possibly get in through the door. So they climbed up onto the roof, cleared away the earth, and broke an opening through. Through the pouring sunlight and the dust, the man lying on the mat was slowly lowered down in front of Jesus.

Seeing their faith, Jesus said to the man lying there, son, your sins are forgiven. The teachers of the law muttered among themselves. This man is blaspheming God. Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said, so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins, get up, pick up your mat, and go home. At once the man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of them all. Everyone was amazed and praised God. We have never seen anything like this.

words.text: Child, your sins are forgiven.
So that you may know the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins, I tell you: get up, take your mat, and go home.
Which is easier: to say your sins are forgiven, or to say get up, take your mat, and walk?

e19.note: Houses in Galilee usually had flat roofs of branches and clay laid over wooden beams, reached by an outside stair. Luke describes the man being let down through the tiles.
e19.reflect: Four friends tore open a roof to lower a paralyzed man down in front of Jesus. Who is someone I want to bring to Jesus but have only been meaning to?

quiz.q: How many men carried the paralyzed man and broke open the roof?
quiz.explain: Mark records that four men carried the paralyzed man (Mk 2:3). They dug through the roof, made an opening, and lowered him down (Mk 2:4).

e19.credit: James Tissot, The Palsied Man Let Down through the Roof, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e20.title: Matthew at the Tax Booth
e20.subtitle: A man who rose from a place of scorn
story: After teaching the crowd by the lake, Jesus set out again. As he passed the tax booth by the road, Levi the son of Alphaeus, that is Matthew, was sitting there. He was a tax collector, who took money from his own people, and whom everyone pointed at and counted among the sinners.

Follow me. It was a single word. Levi got up, left everything behind, and followed him. Then in his own house he held a great banquet for Jesus. Many tax collectors and sinners reclined at the table with Jesus and his disciples. Laughter and the clatter of dishes spilled out beyond the house.

Teachers of the law who belonged to the Pharisees, watching all this, challenged his disciples. Why does your teacher eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners? Jesus heard and answered. It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.

words.text: The healthy do not need a doctor, the sick do. I did not come to call those who think themselves righteous, but sinners.
Follow me.
Go and learn what this means: what I desire is mercy, not sacrifice.

e20.note: Capernaum lay on the road where the Galilee of Herod Antipas met the territory of Philip, so it likely had a toll booth. Tax collectors often took more than was owed and were treated like sinners.
e20.reflect: Jesus called Matthew, the tax collector everyone shunned, and ate with sinners at his house. How might Jesus look at the people I would rather not sit with?

quiz.q: What other name do Mark and Luke use for Matthew the tax collector?
quiz.explain: Matthew's Gospel calls him Matthew (Mt 9:9), while Mark and Luke call him Levi (Mk 2:14; Lk 5:27). Mark identifies him as the son of Alphaeus.

e20.credit: James Tissot, The Calling of Saint Matthew, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e21.title: The Pool of Bethesda
e21.subtitle: The day thirty-eight years of waiting ended
story: At one of the Jewish festivals, Jesus went up to Jerusalem. By the Sheep Gate there was a pool called Bethesda, surrounded by five colonnades. In their shade, crowds of the blind, the lame, and the withered lay packed together. Among them was a man who had been ill for thirty-eight years.

Jesus knew he had been lying there a long time, so he went to him and asked, do you want to get well? Instead of answering, the man poured out his complaint. Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am making my way, someone else always gets down ahead of me. Jesus said to him, get up, pick up your mat, and walk. At once the man was healed, and he picked up his mat and walked.

That day was a Sabbath. The Jewish leaders stopped him. It is not lawful for you to carry your mat on the Sabbath. Because of this, they began to persecute Jesus. Jesus answered them. My Father is still working, and so am I. At that, they tried all the harder to kill him, because he was not only breaking the Sabbath, but calling God his own Father, making himself equal with God.

words.text: Do you want to be made well?
Get up. Pick up your mat and walk.
My Father is still at work even now, and so I am at work too.
Truly I tell you, whoever hears my word and trusts the one who sent me has eternal life, and has already crossed from death into life.

e21.note: Excavations near the Church of Saint Anne in the late nineteenth century uncovered two large reservoirs. Some suggest that colonnades around the four sides and along the wall between the pools would match the five porches John describes.
e21.reflect: When Jesus asked, 'Do you want to be well?', the man began by complaining that he had no one to help him. Even so, Jesus said, 'Get up and walk.' Do I trust his word more than my own circumstances?

quiz.q: How many years had the man Jesus healed at the pool of Bethesda been ill?
quiz.explain: John records that the man had been ill for thirty-eight years (Jn 5:5).

e21.credit: James Tissot, The Piscina Probatica or Pool of Bethesda, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e22.title: Appointing the Twelve
e22.subtitle: Names called after a night of prayer
story: In those days Jesus went up onto a mountain to pray. From sunset, through the rising of the stars, until dawn broke again, he prayed to God all night long. The hillside overlooking the Sea of Galilee was still, and only the sound of the wind brushed through the grass.

When day came, Jesus called his disciples. He called those he wanted, and one by one they came to him. From among them he chose twelve and named them apostles, so that they might be with him, so that he might send them out to proclaim the message, and so that they might have authority to drive out demons.

The names were called one at a time. Simon, who was given the new name Peter, and his brother Andrew. James and John, called the sons of thunder. Philip and Bartholomew, Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, Judas the son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who would one day become the betrayer. Fishermen, a tax collector, a Zealot, people so very different from one another, became one company.

words.text: Jesus went out to the mountain to pray and spent the whole night in prayer to God. When day came, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them.
Jesus called those he wanted, and they came to him. He appointed twelve to be with him and to be sent out to proclaim the message.

e22.note: The number twelve recalls the twelve tribes of Israel. Among the four lists of apostles in the New Testament, Thaddaeus and Judas son of James trade places, and many see them as two names for the same man.
e22.reflect: When Jesus appointed the Twelve, he first called them “to be with him,” and only then sent them out. Before I do anything, how much time do I spend simply staying by his side?

quiz.q: What did Jesus do on the mountain the night before choosing the twelve apostles?
options: He prayed to God all night
quiz.explain: Luke records that Jesus went to the mountain and spent the whole night praying to God, and when day came he chose the twelve (Lk 6:12–13).

e22.credit: James Tissot, Ordaining of the Twelve Apostles, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e23.title: Teaching on the Mountain
e23.subtitle: A voice on the hillside that overturned the world's wisdom
story: People came streaming to a hillside overlooking the Sea of Galilee. When Jesus saw the crowds, he went up on the mountain and sat down, and his disciples came close to him. On that slope, where the wind swept across the grass, he began to speak. Blessed are the poor in spirit, for the kingdom of heaven is theirs.

You are the salt of the earth and the light of the world. Love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you. When you pray, go into your inner room, and pray to your Father, who sees in secret. Look at the birds of the air. See how the lilies of the field grow. So do not worry about tomorrow, but seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness.

The teaching ended with a story of two houses. Everyone who hears my words and does them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock. The rain pours down, the floods rise, the winds beat against it, and that house does not fall. When he finished speaking, the crowds were amazed, because he taught them like one with authority, and not like their teachers of the law.

words.text: Blessed are those who know they have nothing within to lean on. The kingdom of heaven belongs to them.
Love your enemies, and pray for those who torment you. That is how you become children of your Father in heaven.
So do not worry ahead of time about tomorrow. Tomorrow will carry its own worries. Today's trouble is enough for today.
Whoever hears my words and lives by them is like a wise man who built his house on rock. Storms come, and that house still stands.

e23.note: Matthew presents this as a teaching given on a mountain, Luke as one given on a level place. The Church of the Beatitudes on a hill north of the Sea of Galilee was built in 1938, following a tradition that honored this spot as the site of the sermon.
e23.reflect: Jesus said that whoever hears his words and acts on them is like someone who builds a house on rock. What word have I heard for a long time but not yet carried into my life?

quiz.q: Jesus said that whoever hears his words and does them is like someone who built a house where?
quiz.explain: Whoever hears and does these words is like a wise man who built his house on rock, and it did not fall in the storm (Mt 7:24–25). Whoever hears but does not do them is like a house built on sand (Mt 7:26–27).

e23.credit: James Tissot, The Sermon of the Beatitudes, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e24.title: The Centurion's Faith
e24.subtitle: Only say the word
story: In Capernaum there was a centurion. A servant he valued highly was sick and close to death. Hearing about Jesus, the centurion sent some Jewish elders to ask him to come and save his servant. The elders pleaded with Jesus earnestly. This man deserves your help. He loves our nation, and he even built our synagogue for us.

Jesus went with them, and when he was not far from the house, friends sent by the centurion brought his message. Lord, do not trouble yourself. I am not worthy to have you come under my roof. Just say the word. I too am a man under orders, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes.

When Jesus heard this, he was amazed, and he turned to the crowd following him. Not even in Israel have I found faith like this. When the messengers returned to the house, they found the servant already well. Jesus had not even crossed the threshold, yet a single word had reached that house before him.

words.text: I tell you, not even in Israel have I found faith as great as this.
Go. Let it be done for you just as you have believed.
Many will come from east and west and take their places at the feast of the kingdom of heaven with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Lord, I am not one who deserves to have you in my house. Just say one word, and my servant will be healed.

e24.note: A centurion commanded about a hundred soldiers. Galilee was then the territory of Herod Antipas, so this man was most likely a Gentile officer serving under Antipas.
e24.reflect: The centurion trusted Jesus: “I am not worthy. Just say the word.” What am I relying on as I come to him, my own worthiness, or his word?

quiz.q: When the Jewish elders recommended the centurion, what did they say he had built for them?
quiz.explain: The elders said the centurion loved the Jewish nation and had built their synagogue for them (Lk 7:4–5).

e24.credit: James Tissot, The Centurion, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e25.title: The Funeral at Nain
e25.subtitle: A funeral procession halted at the town gate
story: Jesus went to a village called Nain, and his disciples and a large crowd went with him. As he drew near the town gate, a funeral procession was coming out. The dead man was the only son of a widow. Many people of the town walked beside the mother, weeping.

When the Lord saw her, his heart went out to her. Do not weep. Then he stepped forward and touched the bier, and those carrying it stood still. At the town gate, where the wailing had fallen quiet, his voice rang out. Young man, I say to you, get up.

The dead man sat up and began to speak. Jesus gave him back to his mother. Everyone was gripped with awe and gave glory to God. A great prophet has appeared among us. God has come to help his people. This news spread through all of Judea and the surrounding region.

words.text: Do not weep.
Young man, I say to you, get up.
A great prophet has appeared among us. God has come to look after his people.

e25.note: Nain lay at the foot of the Hill of Moreh, and on the far side of that hill was Shunem, where Elisha raised the Shunammite woman's son. That memory may be part of why the people thought of a great prophet.
e25.reflect: No one asked him to, yet Jesus felt compassion for a widow who had lost her only son and stopped the funeral procession. Who near me is quietly weeping these days?

quiz.q: What did Jesus touch before raising the young man?
quiz.explain: Jesus came forward and touched the bier, and those carrying it stood still (Lk 7:14).

e25.credit: James Tissot, The Resurrection of the Widow's Son at Nain, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e26.title: The Woman Who Wet His Feet with Tears
e26.subtitle: One who is forgiven much loves much
story: A Pharisee invited Jesus to eat with him. Jesus went into his house and took his place at the table. The guests reclined around the food, leaning on one side, their feet stretched out behind them. Then there was a stir at the doorway. A woman known in that town as a sinner came in, holding an alabaster jar of perfume close, and stood quietly behind Jesus at his feet.

Her shoulders shook, and she broke into tears. As her falling tears wet the feet of Jesus, she wiped them with her hair, kissed them again and again, and poured the perfume on them. While the fragrance spread through the room, Simon the host watched in silence. If this man were a prophet, he would know what kind of woman is touching him. As if he knew the man's thoughts, Jesus spoke. Simon, I have something to say to you.

Two people owed money. One owed five hundred denarii, the other fifty. If both debts were forgiven, which one will love more? Turning toward the woman, Jesus asked Simon, do you see this woman? You gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears. Then he said to the woman, your sins are forgiven. Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.

words.text: Her many sins have been forgiven, and that is why she has loved so greatly. One who is forgiven little loves little.
Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.
Do you see this woman? When I came into your house, you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears and dried them with her hair.

e26.note: Luke does not give this woman's name. Mary Magdalene is introduced separately in the very next scene, so there is no basis for treating them as the same person. That identification came from an interpretation in the Western church in the late sixth century.
e26.reflect: Saying that the one forgiven much loves much, Jesus welcomed the woman who wet his feet with her tears. When I remember what I have been forgiven, what shape does my love take?

quiz.q: In the parable Jesus told Simon, what debts did the two people owe?
options: Five hundred denarii and fifty denarii
One hundred denarii and ten denarii
One thousand denarii and one hundred denarii
quiz.explain: One owed five hundred denarii and the other fifty, and the lender canceled both debts (Lk 7:41–42).

e26.credit: James Tissot, The Meal in the House of the Pharisee, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e27.title: Parables by the Sea
e27.subtitle: The kingdom of God in a tiny seed
story: That day Jesus went out of the house and sat down by the sea. As people kept crowding in without end, he got into a boat and sat on the water, while the crowd stood packed along the shore. Carried on the calm water, his voice reached far. The murmuring on the shore died away. Listen. A sower went out to sow his seed.

Some seed fell along the path, and the birds came down and pecked it up. Some fell on rocky ground where the soil was thin, and it sprang up quickly, but when the sun rose it was scorched and withered. Some fell among thorns and was choked. But the seed that fell on good soil grew and bore fruit, thirty, sixty, a hundred times over. Whoever has ears, let them hear.

One story followed another. A mustard seed is smaller than any seed sown in the ground, yet it grows into a tree where the birds of the air come and nest in its branches. A little yeast mixed into the flour makes the whole batch rise. A man who finds treasure hidden in a field goes off in joy, sells all he has, and buys that field. So does a merchant who finds a precious pearl. A net thrown into the sea hauls up every kind of fish. That is what the kingdom of heaven was like.

words.text: The seed sown on good soil stands for those who hear the word and welcome it, and they bear fruit thirty, sixty, and a hundred times over.
The kingdom of God is like a mustard seed. When planted it is smaller than any seed, but it grows larger than every plant, and birds nest in its shade.
The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field. Whoever finds it goes off in joy, sells all he has, and buys that field.
Do you light a lamp only to cover it with a bowl or put it under a bed? Will you not set it on a lampstand?

e27.note: Between Capernaum and Tabgha lies a small inlet called the Bay of the Sower. Research suggests its sloping shore gathers sound like a natural amphitheater, so a voice from a boat could reach thousands.
e27.reflect: Jesus said the same seed can be sown, yet the fruit depends on the heart that receives it. These days, when I hear the word, what kind of soil is my heart most like?

quiz.q: Jesus compared the kingdom of heaven to something a woman mixed into three measures of flour until all the dough rose. What was it?
quiz.explain: The kingdom of heaven is like yeast that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour until all of it had risen (Mt 13:33).

e27.credit: James Tissot, Jesus Preaches in a Ship, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e28.title: Rebuking the Wind and the Sea
e28.subtitle: Who is this man?
story: As a day full of parables drew to a close, Jesus said to his disciples, let us cross over to the other side of the lake. Leaving the crowd behind, the disciples took Jesus with them in the boat and rowed out, and other boats followed. Suddenly a fierce squall swept over the lake. Waves broke over the side and poured into the boat.

The boat was filling with water, but Jesus was in the stern, sound asleep on a cushion. The disciples scrambled to him and shook him awake. Teacher, don't you care that we are going to die? Even the voices of fishermen who had cast their nets on this lake all their lives were shaking with fear.

Jesus got up, rebuked the wind, and spoke to the sea. Quiet. Be still. The wind dropped at once, and the lake became as smooth as a mirror. Why are you so afraid? Do you still have no faith? Seized by a fear greater than the sea, the disciples whispered to one another. Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?

words.text: Quiet. Be still.
Why are you so fearful? Do you still have no faith?
Let us cross over to the other side of the lake.
Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?

e28.note: The Sea of Galilee lies in a basin about two hundred ten meters below sea level. When cool air from the surrounding highlands suddenly rushes down the valleys, a calm lake can be whipped into a violent storm in moments.
e28.reflect: After calming the storm, Jesus asked his disciples, “Why are you afraid? Do you still have no faith?” If I heard the same question, how would I answer?

quiz.q: Where in the boat was Jesus sleeping when the storm arose?
options: On the nets in the bow
In the stern, on a cushion
quiz.explain: Mark records that Jesus was asleep on a cushion in the stern, at the back of the boat (Mk 4:38).

e28.credit: James Tissot, Jesus Stilling the Tempest, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e29.title: The Man Among the Tombs
e29.subtitle: A darkness stronger than chains, a word stronger still
story: The boat landed on the far side of the lake, in the region of the Gerasenes. As soon as Jesus stepped out of the boat, a man who lived among the tombs came running out. People had tried to bind him with chains, but he snapped the chains and smashed the shackles. No one could subdue him. Night and day he wandered among the tombs and in the hills, crying out and cutting himself with stones.

He fell down before Jesus and shouted at the top of his voice. Jesus, Son of the Most High God, I beg you, do not torment me. Jesus asked him, what is your name? He answered. Legion, for we are many. On the hillside nearby, a large herd of pigs was feeding. The unclean spirits begged to be sent into them, and when Jesus allowed it, they went in. Then the herd, about two thousand pigs, rushed down the steep bank into the sea and drowned.

The men tending the pigs ran off and reported it, and the whole town came out. What they saw was the man, sitting there, clothed and in his right mind. Instead, the people grew afraid and begged Jesus to leave. As Jesus was getting into the boat, the man pleaded to go with him. Jesus would not allow it, but said, go home and tell them the great things the Lord has done for you. He went all through the Decapolis, telling what Jesus had done for him.

words.text: Go home to your family. Tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and how he has had mercy on you.
Unclean spirit, come out of this man.
What is your name?

e29.note: Mark and Luke call it the region of the Gerasenes, Matthew the region of the Gadarenes, and the manuscripts disagree on the name. At Kursi on the eastern shore stand the remains of a fifth century Byzantine monastery commemorating this event.
e29.reflect: Jesus told the man he had healed not to follow him, but to go home and tell what the Lord had done. What work of the Lord would I like to share with my family and neighbors?

quiz.q: About how many pigs were in the herd the unclean spirits entered?
quiz.explain: Mark records that the herd numbered about two thousand (Mk 5:13). In his account of the same event, Matthew mentions two possessed men (Mt 8:28).

e29.credit: James Tissot, My Name is Legion, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e30.title: Talitha Koum
e30.subtitle: Beyond the news that it was too late
story: When Jesus had crossed back over the lake, Jairus, a leader of the synagogue, pushed through the crowd and fell at his feet. My little daughter is dying. Come and lay your hands on her, and she will live. Jesus set out with him, and a great crowd followed, jostling him from every side. Among them was a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.

She had endured much under many doctors and spent everything she had, yet instead of getting better she only grew worse. If I can just touch his clothes, I will be healed. Keeping low in the press of people, she came up from behind and reached out her hand. At that moment the bleeding stopped, and she felt in her body that she was healed. Jesus turned around and asked, who touched my clothes? Trembling with fear, the woman came forward, fell at his feet, and told him the whole truth. Daughter, your faith has made you well.

While he was still speaking, people came from the synagogue leader's house. Your daughter is dead. Jesus said to the synagogue leader, do not be afraid. Only believe. Jesus took only Peter, James, and John, and the child's father and mother, and went into the room where the child lay. Then he took her by the hand and said, Talitha koum, which means, little girl, get up. At once the twelve-year-old girl got up and walked.

words.text: Talitha koum. Little girl, I say to you, get up.
Do not be afraid. Only believe.
Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace. Be free of your suffering and be whole.
Why all this commotion and weeping? The child is not dead. She is asleep.

e30.note: Talitha koum is Aramaic, the everyday language Jesus spoke. Mark preserves a few of Jesus' Aramaic words just as they sounded, such as Ephphatha, Abba, and Eloi, and then explains their meaning.
e30.reflect: Facing the news that his daughter had died, Jesus told Jairus, “Don't be afraid; just believe.” What do these words say to me about something I think is already too late?

quiz.q: What does Talitha koum, the words Jesus spoke to Jairus's daughter, mean?
quiz.explain: Talitha koum is Aramaic for little girl, get up (Mk 5:41). The girl was twelve years old (Mk 5:42).

e30.credit: James Tissot, The Daughter of Jairus, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e31.title: A Feast in the Wilderness
e31.subtitle: Five barley loaves and two fish
story: The disciples came back from their mission worn out. They crossed by boat toward Bethsaida to a lonely place to rest awhile, but people who had heard the news walked along the shore and got there ahead of them. Jesus had compassion on them, for they were like sheep without a shepherd, and he taught them until the sun was low.

When the disciples suggested sending the crowd away, Jesus' answer took them by surprise. You give them something to eat. The disciples could only look at one another. Philip worked out that even two hundred denarii worth of bread would not be enough, and all Andrew could find was a boy's five barley loaves and two fish. It was spring, close to Passover, and the grass in the fields was green, and the people sat down on it in groups.

Jesus took the bread, looked up to heaven and gave thanks, then broke it and gave it to his disciples. The bread and the fish passed through the disciples' hands to the people without end. The men alone numbered five thousand, and all ate their fill. When they gathered up the leftover pieces, they filled twelve baskets. When the people came to seize him and make him king by force, Jesus withdrew to the mountain alone.

words.text: You yourselves give them something to eat.
Come away by yourselves to a quiet place and rest a little while.
Gather up all the leftover pieces, so that nothing is wasted.

e31.note: It is the only miracle recorded in all four Gospels. Luke names the place as Bethsaida, thought to be near the mouth of the Jordan on the northeast shore of the Sea of Galilee. John notes that the boy's loaves were barley bread, the food of the poor.
e31.reflect: With five barley loaves and two fish that a boy had brought, Jesus fed a huge crowd. What am I holding back from the Lord because it seems too small?

quiz.q: After everyone had eaten, how many baskets of leftover pieces were there?
quiz.explain: When the leftover pieces were gathered, they filled twelve baskets (Mt 14:20; Mk 6:43; Lk 9:17; Jn 6:13). Seven baskets belongs to a different event, the feeding of the four thousand.

e31.credit: James Tissot, The Miracle of the Loaves and Fishes, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e32.title: The One Who Comes Over the Water
e32.when: AD 29, spring · the fourth watch of the night
e32.subtitle: On a windy night, he comes walking on the water
story: After sending the crowd away, Jesus put his disciples into the boat to go ahead of him to the other side, and he went up the mountain alone to pray. As the night deepened, a headwind rose. For hours the disciples rowed in the dark, but in the middle of the lake the boat was tossed this way and that by the waves. The arms gripping the oars grew heavier and heavier.

In the fourth watch of the night, while the sky was still pitch black, someone was walking on the water toward the boat. When the disciples saw him, they cried out in terror that it was a ghost. Through the noise of the wind came a familiar voice. Take heart. It is I. Do not be afraid. Peter called out. Lord, if it is you, tell me to come to you on the water. Jesus said, come.

Peter climbed out of the boat and walked a few steps on the water toward Jesus. But when he saw the strong wind, fear swept over him, and he began to sink. Lord, save me. At once Jesus reached out his hand and caught him. You of little faith, why did you doubt? When the two of them climbed into the boat, the wind died down. The disciples fell down before him. Truly you are the Son of God.

words.text: Take courage. It is I. There is nothing to fear.
Come.
You of little faith, why did you doubt?
You really are the Son of God.

e32.note: In the Roman division of the night, the fourth watch ran from about three to six in the morning. John writes that the disciples saw Jesus after they had rowed twenty-five or thirty stadia, roughly five or six kilometers.
e32.reflect: As Peter began to sink, he cried out, “Lord, save me!” and Jesus immediately reached out and caught him. When fear overwhelms me, what is the first thing I reach for?

quiz.q: Why did Peter begin to sink while walking on the water?
options: He saw the wind and was afraid
He looked back at the boat
quiz.explain: When Peter saw the wind, he was afraid and began to sink (Mt 14:30).

e32.credit: James Tissot, Jesus Walks on the Sea, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e33.title: I Am the Bread of Life
e33.subtitle: A deeper food for those who came looking for a full stomach
story: The next day, the crowd that had eaten the bread came by boat to Capernaum, looking for Jesus. Teacher, when did you get here? Jesus saw right through them. You are looking for me not because you saw signs, but because you ate the bread and were filled. Do not work for food that spoils, but for the food that lasts to eternal life.

The people brought up the manna their ancestors had eaten in the wilderness. Isn't it written that they ate bread from heaven? Jesus answered. The true bread that comes down from heaven and gives life to the world, the bread of life, is me. The bread I will give is my flesh. A murmur spread through the synagogue in Capernaum. Isn't this Joseph's son? How can he give us his flesh to eat?

Even among his disciples there was grumbling. This teaching is too hard. Who can accept it? From that day on, many of his disciples turned back and no longer walked with him. Jesus turned to the twelve who remained. Do you want to leave too? After a moment of silence, Peter spoke. Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.

words.text: I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty again.
Do not toil for food that soon disappears. Work for the food that endures to eternal life.
Do you want to go away as well?
Lord, you have the words of eternal life. Who else could we go to?

e33.note: The white limestone synagogue that stands in Capernaum today is thought to date from the fourth century or later, but the black basalt foundation beneath it may be a trace of the synagogue of Jesus' day.
e33.reflect: Jesus said, “I am the bread of life,” yet many left, wanting only bread. What do I want from Jesus, the things he gives, or Jesus himself?

quiz.q: Where did Jesus teach about the bread of life?
options: In the Temple courts in Jerusalem
In a boat on the shore of the Sea of Galilee
quiz.explain: Jesus said these things while teaching in the synagogue at Capernaum (Jn 6:59).

e33.credit: James Tissot, You Follow Me for the Miracles, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e34.title: A Mother from the Region of Tyre
e34.subtitle: A faith content with crumbs
story: Jesus left Galilee and went north into the region of Tyre, a foreign land by the sea. He stayed in a house and wanted no one to know, but he could not stay hidden. A woman who heard about him came at once and fell at his feet. Her little daughter was tormented by an unclean spirit. She was not an Israelite, but a Greek woman, born in Syrian Phoenicia.

Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me. When Jesus gave her not a single word in reply, she kept following and crying out, and the disciples asked him to send her away, since she was bothering them. Jesus' answer sounded cold. It is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs. Still the mother would not back away.

Yes, Lord. But even the dogs under the table eat the crumbs the children drop. After a moment, Jesus looked at her. Woman, your faith is great. Let it be done for you as you wish. When she went home, she found the child lying peacefully on the bed, and the spirit that had tormented her was already gone.

words.text: Woman, your faith is truly great. Let it be done for you just as you wish.
Let the children be fed first. It is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the house dogs.
Because you have answered this way, go home now. The evil spirit has already left your daughter.
Yes, Lord. But even the dogs under the table eat the crumbs the children drop, do they not?

e34.note: Tyre was a Phoenician port city on the Mediterranean coast, Gentile territory in Jewish eyes. The word Jesus used refers not to wild dogs but to small dogs kept in the house.
e34.reflect: Even when Jesus seemed not to answer, the foreign woman held on to the end for her daughter's sake. What do I do with prayers that seem to go unanswered?

quiz.q: How does the Gospel of Mark describe this woman?
options: A Greek, born in Syrian Phoenicia
The wife of a Roman centurion
The wife of a Galilean fisherman
quiz.explain: Mark describes her as a Greek woman, Syrophoenician by birth (Mk 7:26), while Matthew calls her a Canaanite woman (Mt 15:22).

e34.credit: James Tissot, The Canaanite's Daughter, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e35.title: Ephphatha — Be Opened
e35.subtitle: The day closed ears and a bound tongue were set free
story: Jesus left Tyre and went by way of Sidon, taking the long way around through the region of the Decapolis, and came to the Sea of Galilee. People brought him a man who was deaf and could hardly speak, and begged him to lay his hand on him. Jesus took him aside, away from the crowd, to a quiet place. The noise of the people faded into the distance.

Jesus put his fingers into the man's ears, then spat and touched his tongue. Then, looking up to heaven, he sighed deeply and said a single word. Ephphatha. Be opened. At that, the blocked ears were opened and the bound tongue was set free. He began to speak clearly. It was a voice that had been locked away for a long time.

Jesus told them to tell no one, but the more he forbade it, the more widely they spread the news. The people were utterly astonished and said, he has done everything well. He even makes the deaf hear and the mute speak. When Jesus went up on a mountain, people brought the lame, the blind, the mute, and many others who were sick, and laid them at his feet. Seeing those who had been healed, the crowd was amazed and gave glory to the God of Israel.

words.text: Ephphatha. Be opened!
Everything he does is wonderful. He makes the deaf hear and the mute speak.

e35.note: Ephphatha is Aramaic, the everyday language of Judea in Jesus' time, and Mark often preserves such Aramaic expressions as they were spoken. The Decapolis was a region of ten Greek-style cities scattered east and south of the Sea of Galilee.
e35.reflect: When Jesus healed a man who could not hear or speak, people were amazed and said, “He has done everything well.” How often do I remember the good the Lord has done for me and give thanks?

quiz.q: What does the word Ephphatha, spoken by Jesus, mean?
quiz.explain: Mark explains that Ephphatha means 'Be opened' (Mk 7:34).

e35.credit: James Tissot, Jesus Heals the Blind and Lame on the Mountain, c. 1886–1894 · Brooklyn Museum · Public domain

e36.title: Who Do You Say I Am?
e36.subtitle: A question asked beneath the rock where the spring bursts out
story: The villages of Caesarea Philippi, at the foot of Mount Hermon, where a stream of the Jordan springs from beneath the rock. It was a long road north from Galilee. Jesus had been praying alone, and as he walked that road with his disciples, he slowed his pace and asked, who do people say I am? The disciples looked at one another.

Some say John the Baptist, others say Elijah. Others say Jeremiah, or one of the prophets. Jesus asked again. But who do you say I am? Peter answered. You are the Christ, the Son of the living God. Jesus said, blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah. You are Peter, the rock.

From then on Jesus began to make it plain that he must go up to Jerusalem, suffer many things at the hands of the elders, the chief priests, and the teachers of the law, be killed, and on the third day be raised. When Peter took hold of him and protested that this could not happen, Jesus turned and rebuked him sharply. Get behind me, Satan. Then he said to them all, whoever wants to follow me must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.

words.text: But you, what about you? Who do you say that I am?
Whoever wants to follow me must let go of self, take up their cross, and come after me.
